subject: Aurora Health - request for special availability pathway and operational implications
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora Health - initial ask for special availability pathway and runtime impact

Hi team,

Sophie at Aurora Health sent a follow-up to our trial that escalates their ask: they want a contractual availability commitment that is higher than our standard offering for a set of endpoints tied to a production integration (clinical decision support). Specifically they are asking for a P95 latency SLA of <= 120ms and an availability commitment of 99.995% for read traffic to pinned model instances (multi-region failover). They also asked for a dedicated routing policy so requests from their production traffic always hit their reserved pool where possible.

I attached the customer-facing SLA draft and their requested runbook. Key constraints I want us to evaluate before we respond:
- What does a 99.995% availability promise look like in our three-tier product surface (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)?
- For Dedicated: what additional warm pool or capacity reservation is required to maintain P95 <= 120ms at their projected QPS (attached)?
- What operational runbook items (monitoring, guardrails, on-call escalation, automated fallback) do we need to guarantee this?
- Any impact on batching/cache strategies (will we need to reduce batching or disable certain cache optimizations to hit latency)?

Ask: please provide a short one-paragraph impact summary + an estimated cost delta (relative to their committed monthly spend) and a list of non-negotiable runbook items. We need this to build an internal recommendation for Jonas and to feed to Finance/Legal if we proceed. Aurora wants an answer before their vendor review on Aug 6th.

Attachments: aurora_sla_draft_v1.pdf, aurora_runbook_v1.xlsx, cost_delta_estimations.csv

Thanks,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora Health - initial ask for special availability pathway and runtime impact

Thanks Irene — adding context from my side: Aurora is in the late stages of procurement. They have a pilot contract already and are prepared to move to a 12-month committed plan if we can sign off on the availability/latency carveouts. The procurement team shared their vendor review timeline (needs internal sign-off on our commitments by Aug 6th).

From commercial: they are targeting a committed monthly spend of $95k/month for the Dedicated deployment. They asked whether we can include a small quarterly credit if we miss the custom p95 target during the first 90 days. They also requested a templated runbook they can review.

Immediate asks for Engineering/Platform:
- A short note on whether 120ms P95 is feasible with our current runtime on the recommended GPU types (NVIDIA A10/A100) for their mix of short chat-like prompts (avg seq len ~60 tokens) and a smaller subset of longer context calls.
- Rough incremental cost to maintain a dedicated warm pool and multi-region active standby.

Irene: once we have the impact summary, I recommend we propose a provisional SLA in the draft with conditional terms (90-day probation + credits structure) while we finalize the operational runbook.

-M

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts (Sales)
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora Health - initial ask for special availability pathway and runtime impact

Irene/Marissa — reviewed the attachments and ran a quick simulation based on their QPS profile. Short summary:

Feasibility:
- 120ms P95 for their short prompts is achievable on Dedicated A100-backed instances if we: (a) reserve warm instances per region (no cold starts), (b) pin model shards to instance groups and avoid cross-host KV fetches for hot paths, and (c) tune batching to a small max batch size (e.g., 8) with strong latency-first scheduling.
- 99.995% availability (~4.38 minutes of downtime/year) for a single-region setup is very risky; to approach that SLA we need active-active multi-region with automated failover and capacity headroom. That implies at least 2x steady-state capacity across 2 regions + additional buffer for burst.

Operational requirements / non-negotiables:
- Dedicated warm pool per region with pre-warmed model pinned instances.
- Persistent KV cache affinity per client namespace to avoid cross-host cache misses during failover.
- Fast health-checks + traffic shifting automation with staged ramp (10%, 50%, 100%) and canary routing for changes.
- 24/7 on-call escalation (SRE) with runbook steps for traffic failover and rollback.
- A documented acceptance test harness (synthetic traffic + smoke checks) that runs every deploy to prove P95 targets.

Cost / capacity notes:
- Rough incremental compute delta: ~1.8x baseline (steady-state multiplier) to support warm pools + multi-region standby for their projected QPS. I attached a quick cost_delta_estimations.csv — ballpark extra $38k-55k/month depending on instance class and cross-region egress.
- There will be feature trade-offs: to guarantee latency at scale we should limit aggressive batching, which increases token-cost per request. Also some caching optimizations (prefix compression) become less effective with strict per-tenant affinity.

Risks:
- Multi-region active-active increases complexity for KV cache consistency and billing attribution.
- We may need contractual carveouts describing reasonable maintenance windows and a clear definition of what constitutes availability (control-plane vs data-plane).

Happy to build a short runbook draft from the attached and work with Infra to quantify costs more precisely.

-marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora Health - initial ask for special availability pathway and runtime impact

Thanks all for the quick turnaround. Based on Marcus's summary and the commercial signals from Marissa, I approve a provisional exception path for Aurora Health under the following conditions:

1) We offer a conditional SLA in the contract that is staged: 90-day probation during which the effective SLA is 99.95% with a monthly credit ladder for any P95 misses; after successful probation (no more than one incident impacting P95 in 90 days) we upgrade to the requested 99.995% availability with an agreed credit schedule.
2) Aurora must accept the operational runbook (to be finalized) which includes the dedicated warm pools, synthetic acceptance tests per deploy, and a committed on-call SRE escalation path.
3) Finance will approve a pricing uplift equal to the estimated incremental capacity cost + a managed services surcharge (Marcus's delta + 20%). Marissa, please start the uplift approval with Finance and copy me.
4) Legal to sign off on maintenance window carveouts and a clear definition of availability (data-plane only; control-plane incidents excluded).

Jonas requests that we provide the customer with a clearly labeled "provisional SLA" attachment (not final) and a DocuSign envelope for the provisional terms. We will not finalize the firm 99.995% commitment until after the probation period and a full ops readiness review.

Next steps:
- Marcus: please produce a short ops runbook bullet list and a firm cost estimate by Aug 3.
- Marissa: prepare the provisional SLA draft and credit ladder; coordinate with Finance & Legal.
- Irene: coordinate a brief with Aurora and share the provisional SLA (DocuSign link below) so they can start internal approvals.

DocuSign (provisional): https://app.docusign.com/prepare?envelopeId=5f7b3a2d
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/AH-2026-0593

If we meet the Aug 6 vendor review ask with these provisional documents, we'll move to a detailed runbook + final contract.

Jonas
